title: React + Redux Project Setup + Tailwind

introduction.heading: Setting Up a Modern React & Redux Project with Vite
introduction.description: A complete guide to scaffolding a production-ready React application with Redux state management, Tailwind CSS, routing, and folder structure. This covers the essential packages and configurations needed to start developing immediately.

prerequisites: Basic familiarity with npm and command line

steps.title: Create a Vite React Project
steps.description: Use Vite to scaffold a new React project. Vite is much faster than Create React App and is the modern standard for new React projects.
steps.note: Replace 'frontend' with your desired project name. The --template react flag ensures you get a React setup.

steps.title: Navigate to Project & Install Dependencies
steps.description: Enter the project directory and install the base dependencies that come with Vite React.

steps.title: Install Redux State Management
steps.description: Redux Toolkit simplifies Redux setup with less boilerplate. react-redux binds Redux to React components via hooks.
steps.note: Redux Toolkit includes Redux, Redux Thunk for async actions, and Immer for immutable updates.

steps.title: Install Tailwind CSS with Vite Plugin (Optional)
steps.description: Tailwind CSS provides utility-first styling. The @tailwindcss/vite plugin enables faster builds with Vite.

steps.title: Configure Tailwind in vite.config.js (Optional)
steps.description: Add the Tailwind plugin to your Vite configuration for proper PostCSS processing.
steps.note: The order matters: tailwindcss() should come before react().

steps.title: Add the Tailwind Import to CSS (Optional)
steps.description: Update your main CSS file (usually src/index.css) to pull in Tailwind. Tailwind v4 replaced the old three-line @tailwind base/components/utilities directives with a single @import statement.
steps.note: Replace any existing CSS content in your main CSS file with this import - if you're following a Tailwind v3 tutorial, you'll see @tailwind base/components/utilities instead, which no longer works with @tailwindcss/vite.

steps.title: Install React Router for Navigation
steps.description: React Router enables client-side routing for multi-page navigation without server requests.

steps.title: Create Redux Store Structure
steps.description: Set up your Redux store with slices. Create a store.js file to configure Redux.
steps.note: You'll add more slices (reducer files) as you build features.

steps.title: Wrap Your App with Redux Provider
steps.description: Connect Redux to your React app by wrapping the root component with the Redux Provider.

steps.title: Create Routes with React Router
steps.description: Set up basic routing in your App component.

steps.title: Optional: Add Development Tools
steps.description: Install packages that improve development experience (ESLint, Prettier, Redux DevTools).
steps.note: ESLint finds bugs, Prettier formats code. Redux DevTools helps debug Redux state changes.

steps.title: Optional: Environment Variables Setup
steps.description: Create a .env.local file for API keys and environment-specific configuration (not committed to git).
steps.note: In Vite, variables must start with VITE_ to be accessible in the client. Access them as import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL

folderStructure.heading: Recommended Folder Structure
folderStructure.description: This structure scales well for medium-sized applications:
folderStructure.structure:
frontend/
├── src/
│   ├── components/        # Reusable React components
│   │   ├── Header.jsx
│   │   ├── Footer.jsx
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── pages/             # Full page components
│   │   ├── Home.jsx
│   │   ├── About.jsx
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── redux/             # Redux state management
│   │   ├── store.js
│   │   ├── slices/        # Redux slices
│   │   │   ├── userSlice.js
│   │   │   ├── authSlice.js
│   │   │   └── ...
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── hooks/             # Custom React hooks
│   │   ├── useAuth.js
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── utils/             # Utility functions
│   │   ├── api.js         # API calls
│   │   ├── constants.js
│   │   └── helpers.js
│   ├── styles/            # Global styles
│   │   └── globals.css
│   ├── App.jsx
│   ├── main.jsx
│   └── index.css
├── public/
├── .env.local             # Environment variables (gitignored)
├── .env.example           # Template for .env.local
├── .gitignore
├── vite.config.js
├── package.json
└── README.md

backendSetup.heading: Optional: Backend Project Setup
backendSetup.description: If you need a backend server (Node.js/Express), create it alongside your frontend:

categories.title: API & Data Fetching
items: axios (npm install axios) - Promise-based HTTP client
React Query / TanStack Query - Server state management

categories.title: Code Quality & Formatting
items: husky (pre-commit hooks) - Run tests before committing

categories.title: Testing
items: React Testing Library (npm install --save-dev @testing-library/react) - Component testing

categories.title: UI & Styling
items: Headless UI (npm install @headlessui/react) - Accessible UI components
React Icons (npm install react-icons) - Icon library
Framer Motion (npm install framer-motion) - Animation library

categories.title: Development & Debugging
items: Redux DevTools (npm install redux-devtools) - Debug Redux state
React Developer Tools (browser extension) - React debugging
Vite Plugin Inspect - Analyze Vite plugins

categories.title: TypeScript (Optional but Recommended)
items: Create project with: npm create vite@latest frontend -- --template react-ts
Strongly typed Redux actions and reducers
